content:
Last month there were reports that Apple is developing a brand-new, AI-powered shopping assistant for the Apple Store app on iPhone and iPad.

The company now appears to be rolling out this feature to some users in an "early access" form.

Inside the Apple Store app, some users will now see a new chat-style icon in the bottom-right corner, replacing the traditional search icon. On that page, users can search for products, or start a conversation with a "virtual shopping assistant".

Suggested prompts offered by the system include:

  • Latest Apple products
  • Check my trade-in value
  • Explain carrier offers
  • Help me pick a watch
  • iPhone monthly installment plans
  • Compare iPad models

The image above was provided by X user ShrimpApplePro, giving us an early look at the new design.

Apple's fine print notes:

Not everyone can use the shopping assistant inside the Apple Store app. Apple says it is currently only open to some users in an "early access" form. As for when it will roll out fully, no timeline has been given.

What do you think about Apple adding a brand-new AI assistant to the Apple Store app? Would you use it? Let us know in the comments.
